spec.description: Every nuclear power reactor in the world, from Obninsk in 1954 to the 435 in service at the end of 2023, entering service and shutting down year by year with a time brush that plays them (GeoNuclearData, from the IAEA's PRIS), and the electricity they made country by country, 1965 to 2025 (Our World in Data). The boom of the 1970s and 1980s, China since 2000, Japan after Fukushima, Germany's exit.

spec.rawSql:
-- Their net capacity, in GW.
WITH w AS (SELECT coalesce(try_cast($t_lo AS TIMESTAMP), TIMESTAMP '1954-01-01') AS lo,
                  coalesce(try_cast($t_hi AS TIMESTAMP), TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01') AS hi)
SELECT coalesce(sum(capacity_mw), 0) / 1000 AS "GW in service" FROM $reactors, w
WHERE started < w.hi AND (shut_down IS NULL OR shut_down >= w.hi) AND ($country = '' OR country = $country)

-- Reactors that entered commercial operation during the window.
WITH w AS (SELECT coalesce(try_cast($t_lo AS TIMESTAMP), TIMESTAMP '1954-01-01') AS lo,
                  coalesce(try_cast($t_hi AS TIMESTAMP), TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01') AS hi)
SELECT count(*)::DOUBLE AS "Entered service" FROM $reactors, w
WHERE started >= w.lo AND started < w.hi AND ($country = '' OR country = $country)

spec.description: Reactors that entered commercial operation during the window (pale yellow on the map).

options.content:
### Reactors and the electricity they made

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Reactors** | [GeoNuclearData](https://github.com/cristianst85/GeoNuclearData) (Cristian Stoica, ODbL 1.0), which follows the IAEA's [Power Reactor Information System](https://pris.iaea.org) (PRIS) and the World Nuclear Association, at its update of 2 March 2024: 804 reactors, 759 with a place |
| **In service** | From a reactor's commercial operation to its permanent shutdown. A reactor idle but not shut down for good stays in service, as most of Japan's did after Fukushima (21 were listed as in suspended operation in 2024): the chart of the electricity they made shows the difference |
| **Left out** | Nine reactors that ran have no date of commercial operation in the list, Palisades among them; they stay off the timeline. Under construction is as of March 2024 |
| **Places** | Approximate: a plant's units share one point |
| **Capacity** | Design net capacity, in MWe |
| **Electricity** | [Our World in Data](https://github.com/owid/energy-data) (CC BY 4.0), based on the Energy Institute's Statistical Review of World Energy and Ember: nuclear electricity by country, 1965 to 2025, and its share of each country's electricity. The rest of the world is the World's total less the countries drawn |
| **Built by** | `datasets/nuclear-power/build.sh` in [pacha-dashboards](https://github.com/ubica-ecuador/pacha-dashboards): DuckDB reads both sources and writes two Parquet files |

spec.rawSql:
-- The years the brush is drawn over: GW entering commercial operation each year in the country picked (or
-- every country), every country in grey behind, and the GW in service on each January 1st (a line).
WITH years AS (SELECT unnest(generate_series(TIMESTAMP '1954-01-01', TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01', INTERVAL 1 YEAR)) AS "time"),
r AS (SELECT started, shut_down, capacity_mw, (($country = '' OR country = $country)) AS keep FROM $reactors WHERE started IS NOT NULL)
SELECT y."time",
       coalesce(sum(r.capacity_mw) FILTER (WHERE date_trunc('year', r.started) = y."time"), 0) / 1000 AS "Every country",
       coalesce(sum(r.capacity_mw) FILTER (WHERE r.keep AND date_trunc('year', r.started) = y."time"), 0) / 1000 AS "GW entering service",
       coalesce(sum(r.capacity_mw) FILTER (WHERE r.keep AND r.started < y."time" AND (r.shut_down IS NULL OR r.shut_down >= y."time")), 0) / 1000 AS "GW in service"
FROM years AS y, r
GROUP BY y."time"
ORDER BY y."time"

spec.description: The window every view takes: drag it, resize it by its handles or draw a new one, step it year by year, or press play to run the years. Bars: GW entering service each year (in grey, every country, once one is picked); line: GW in service on January 1st.
spec.title: Years: brush or play

spec.rawSql:
-- GW in service at the end of the window, by country: already in service when it opened, and entered
-- during it. Every country: this is where one is picked.
WITH w AS (SELECT coalesce(try_cast($t_lo AS TIMESTAMP), TIMESTAMP '1954-01-01') AS lo,
                  coalesce(try_cast($t_hi AS TIMESTAMP), TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01') AS hi)
SELECT country,
       round(coalesce(sum(capacity_mw) FILTER (WHERE started < w.lo), 0) / 1000, 2) AS gw_before,
       round(coalesce(sum(capacity_mw) FILTER (WHERE started >= w.lo), 0) / 1000, 2) AS gw_new
FROM $reactors, w
WHERE started < w.hi AND (shut_down IS NULL OR shut_down >= w.hi)
GROUP BY country
ORDER BY gw_before + gw_new DESC
LIMIT 12

spec.description: The 12 countries with the most nuclear capacity in service at the end of the time brush's window, in GW: already in service when it opened (orange) and entered during it (pale yellow). Click a country to follow it on the map, the cards and the time brush; click it again to let go.
spec.title: Who has the power: GW in service at the window's end

spec.rawSql:
-- Nuclear electricity, year by year, in TWh: the seven countries that made the most in any year, the one
-- picked in the ranking if it is not among them, and the rest of the world (the World's total less theirs).
-- Every group has a value every year, so the areas stack.
WITH top AS (SELECT country, max(twh) AS peak FROM $generation WHERE country <> 'World' GROUP BY country ORDER BY peak DESC LIMIT 7),
named AS (SELECT country, peak FROM top
          UNION SELECT country, max(twh) FROM $generation WHERE country = $country AND country NOT IN (SELECT country FROM top) GROUP BY country),
ranked AS (SELECT country, row_number() OVER (ORDER BY peak DESC) AS ord FROM named),
world AS (SELECT "time", twh FROM $generation WHERE country = 'World'),
grid AS (SELECT world."time", ranked.country, ranked.ord FROM world, ranked),
countries AS (SELECT grid."time", grid.country AS grp, coalesce(g.twh, 0) AS twh, grid.ord
              FROM grid LEFT JOIN $generation AS g ON g.country = grid.country AND g."time" = grid."time")
SELECT "time", grp, twh, ord FROM countries
UNION ALL
SELECT world."time", 'Rest of the world', greatest(world.twh - coalesce(sum(c.twh), 0), 0), 99
FROM world LEFT JOIN countries AS c ON c."time" = world."time"
GROUP BY world."time", world.twh
ORDER BY "time", ord

-- The share of electricity from nuclear power, in %: the World's, or the picked country's.
SELECT "time", share FROM $generation
WHERE country = CASE WHEN $country = '' THEN 'World' ELSE $country END AND share IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY "time"

spec.description: Nuclear electricity each year, in TWh, for the seven countries that made the most and the rest of the world, with the share of the world's electricity from nuclear power (dashed, right axis); a country picked in the ranking shows its own. The time brush's window is shaded. Our World in Data, from the Energy Institute and Ember.
spec.title: The electricity they made, 1965 to 2025

options.content:
- **1954:** Obninsk, near Moscow, is the first nuclear plant to feed a grid: 5 MW.
- **The boom:** 159 reactors entered service in the 1970s and 228 in the 1980s, 41 in 1985 alone. The 1990s brought 53.
- **Since 2000:** 120 more, 52 of them in China.
- **Fukushima, March 2011:** Japan's reactors made 292 TWh in 2010 and none in 2014; 94 in 2025. Most were idled, not shut down for good, so on the map they stay lit.
- **Germany** shut 8 reactors in August 2011 and its last three on 15 April 2023.
- **Today:** a record 2,812 TWh in 2025, yet nuclear's share of the world's electricity has halved since its 1996 peak, from 17.4 % to 8.9 %.

*Press play at the bottom to run the years: pale yellow, a reactor entering service; red, one shutting down; grey, shut earlier; blue rings, under construction in 2024. Click a country in the ranking to follow it.*

spec.rawSql:
-- In service when the window opened and still at its end.
WITH w AS (SELECT coalesce(try_cast($t_lo AS TIMESTAMP), TIMESTAMP '1954-01-01') AS lo,
                  coalesce(try_cast($t_hi AS TIMESTAMP), TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01') AS hi)
SELECT name, country, reactor_type AS type, capacity_mw AS mwe,
       CASE WHEN shut_down IS NOT NULL THEN strftime(started, '%b %Y') || ' – ' || strftime(shut_down, '%b %Y')
            WHEN status = 'Suspended Operation' THEN 'since ' || strftime(started, '%b %Y') || ', idle in March 2024'
            ELSE 'since ' || strftime(started, '%b %Y') END AS service,
       latitude, longitude
FROM $reactors, w
WHERE started < w.lo AND (shut_down IS NULL OR shut_down >= w.hi) AND ($country = '' OR country = $country)

-- Entered commercial operation during the window and still in service at its end.
WITH w AS (SELECT coalesce(try_cast($t_lo AS TIMESTAMP), TIMESTAMP '1954-01-01') AS lo,
                  coalesce(try_cast($t_hi AS TIMESTAMP), TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01') AS hi)
SELECT name, country, reactor_type AS type, capacity_mw AS mwe,
       CASE WHEN shut_down IS NOT NULL THEN strftime(started, '%b %Y') || ' – ' || strftime(shut_down, '%b %Y')
            WHEN status = 'Suspended Operation' THEN 'since ' || strftime(started, '%b %Y') || ', idle in March 2024'
            ELSE 'since ' || strftime(started, '%b %Y') END AS service,
       latitude, longitude
FROM $reactors, w
WHERE started >= w.lo AND started < w.hi AND (shut_down IS NULL OR shut_down >= w.hi) AND ($country = '' OR country = $country)

-- Shut down for good during the window.
WITH w AS (SELECT coalesce(try_cast($t_lo AS TIMESTAMP), TIMESTAMP '1954-01-01') AS lo,
                  coalesce(try_cast($t_hi AS TIMESTAMP), TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01') AS hi)
SELECT name, country, reactor_type AS type, capacity_mw AS mwe,
       CASE WHEN shut_down IS NOT NULL THEN strftime(started, '%b %Y') || ' – ' || strftime(shut_down, '%b %Y')
            WHEN status = 'Suspended Operation' THEN 'since ' || strftime(started, '%b %Y') || ', idle in March 2024'
            ELSE 'since ' || strftime(started, '%b %Y') END AS service,
       latitude, longitude
FROM $reactors, w
WHERE shut_down >= w.lo AND shut_down < w.hi AND ($country = '' OR country = $country)

-- Shut down for good before the window.
WITH w AS (SELECT coalesce(try_cast($t_lo AS TIMESTAMP), TIMESTAMP '1954-01-01') AS lo,
                  coalesce(try_cast($t_hi AS TIMESTAMP), TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01') AS hi)
SELECT name, country, reactor_type AS type, capacity_mw AS mwe,
       CASE WHEN shut_down IS NOT NULL THEN strftime(started, '%b %Y') || ' – ' || strftime(shut_down, '%b %Y')
            WHEN status = 'Suspended Operation' THEN 'since ' || strftime(started, '%b %Y') || ', idle in March 2024'
            ELSE 'since ' || strftime(started, '%b %Y') END AS service,
       latitude, longitude
FROM $reactors, w
WHERE shut_down < w.lo AND ($country = '' OR country = $country)

-- Under construction in March 2024, once the window reaches 2024.
WITH w AS (SELECT coalesce(try_cast($t_lo AS TIMESTAMP), TIMESTAMP '1954-01-01') AS lo,
                  coalesce(try_cast($t_hi AS TIMESTAMP), TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01') AS hi)
SELECT name, country, reactor_type AS type, capacity_mw AS mwe, 'Under construction in March 2024' AS service, latitude, longitude
FROM $reactors, w
WHERE status = 'Under Construction' AND w.hi >= TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01' AND ($country = '' OR country = $country)

A country picked in the ranking keeps only its reactors. Hover a reactor for its name and years.
